Terms and responsible reuse

How to use, cite and reuse this resource without changing the meaning of the evidence.

01

What this resource is

This is a public evidence resource developed and maintained by CauseWay to support evidence-informed decision-making. It is not a government publication, regulatory instruction or substitute for an original source. Original publishers remain the authoritative source for the data and publications they issue. CauseWay is responsible for its own synthesis, derivations and presentation. Citing or linking to a source does not imply that the source institution endorses CauseWay’s analysis. This resource does not confirm whether any named institution is currently licensed or operating. Nothing on this resource is financial, legal or regulatory advice, or confirmation of any institution’s current status.

02

Reuse

This resource contains CauseWay-authored summaries and derived outputs alongside third-party source material. Reuse of source material depends on the original publisher’s terms; this resource does not yet record item-level reuse terms. Where permission to redistribute or adapt source material is not stated, do not assume that permission exists. Source-specific restrictions continue to apply to underlying data, tables, figures and text.

03

Preserve evidence meaning

Do not remove the period, unit, applicable population or source limitation in a way that changes the meaning of a figure. Targets must remain targets; historical evidence must remain historical; evidence limited to part of the population, an area or a programme must not be presented as a national fact.

04

Citation

Cite the original source. Where CauseWay’s processing, calculation or synthesis materially shapes the result, cite the relevant evidence record or analytical reading as well.

05

Rights stay with the source

Availability on this resource does not grant rights that the underlying source has not granted.
